executive_summary.headline: Critical shipping chokepoints—Strait of Hormuz transit down 94% year-on-year and Bab el-Mandeb down 34%—combined with low Rhine levels and elevated EU energy prices are driving AMBER world risk.
executive_summary.next_step: Within 48 hours, map which suppliers and end-markets depend on Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb routes; cross-check against current inventory buffers and lead times to quantify exposure to further transit delays.
executive_summary.context: The Strait of Hormuz transit collapse (94% decline week-to-8-Nov) is the primary driver. Bab el-Mandeb transits are also materially down 34% year-on-year, signaling sustained Red Sea congestion. Rhine water levels remain constrained (Kaub 16 cm, Maxau 363 cm), and EU natural gas is 131% above September 2025 baseline, raising energy costs for inbound and processing operations. Macro, suppliers and peers pillars are all GREEN; world pillar alone is AMBER.
